entities.summary:
Posidonius 'of Apamea' or 'of Rhodes', was a Greek politician, astronomer, astrologer, geographer, historian, mathematician, and teacher native to Apamea, Syria. He was considered the most learned man of his time and, possibly, of the entire Stoic school.

Born in Apamea around 135 BCE, Posidonius was a polymath who excelled in various fields. He was a prominent Stoic philosopher, and his work in astronomy and mathematics was highly regarded. He also made significant contributions to the fields of geography and history. Posidonius was a prolific writer and teacher, and his teachings were widely sought after. He was known for his ability to synthesize complex ideas and present them in a clear and concise manner.

Despite his many achievements, Posidonius's life was marked by controversy. He was accused of promoting a form of Stoicism that was seen as too liberal by some. Additionally, he was criticized for his views on the nature of the universe, which were seen as too radical by some of his contemporaries.

Today, Posidonius is remembered as one of the most important Stoic philosophers of the Hellenistic period. His work continues to be studied by scholars today, and his legacy as a polymath and teacher remains unchallenged.

The most famous quote from Posidonius is: "The universe is a single, living being, and we are a part of it."
